requirement:
The view of {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.file_map.notes` MUST show
each `habeas:coverage` citation attached to the file root or an explicitly
declared function or method. Each entry MUST identify its source item and
source location and show the fenced citation commentary and Rust doc comments
supplying its tracked justification under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.exceptions.anchor`.
When no tracked justification is present, the entry MUST say so.

File-root citations MUST be labelled as file-threshold exception proposals;
function and method citations MUST be labelled as function exception proposals,
following {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.exceptions.anchor`.
rationale: The tests in `src/execution_coverage/notes.rs` adequately check `requirements.test-coverage.index.file_map.notes.justifications`. I read the whole file, including the `pages`/`entry` rendering code and the test helpers `fixture` and `render`. I used the code only to see how the tests run. I took the expected behaviour from the requirement text. **Obligations and the tests that cover them** - **Show each `habeas:coverage` citation on the file root or an explicitly declared function or method.** - `notes_show_root_function_and_method_proposals_with_owned_commentary_and_docs` has a root citation in `//!` fenced commentary, a free function, an `impl` method and an unexplained function. It asserts all four entries appear, with headings `File root`, `fn[ordinary]`, `impl[Worker]/fn[work]` and `fn[unexplained]`. - The same test shows a citation on a nested `mod` does not become a file-root exception. It asserts `Nested module must` is absent and that the file-threshold label appears exactly once. - It also asserts child documentation does not leak into the root entry. - `citations_on_modules_and_citation_text_in_literals_do_not_create_explanations` shows a module-only citation and `{cite}` text inside a string literal produce no entry. It asserts the "No coverage explanations are present" message and that no "exception proposal" label appears. - **Each entry identifies its source item and source location.** The first test checks, for each of the four entries, the exact `Source: code.rs:{first}–{last}` range and `First source citation at line {n}.`. The item heading is checked in the same test. - **Show fenced citation commentary and Rust doc comments that supply the justification.** - The first test shows both together on one item, with `///` docs plus fenced commentary on `ordinary`. It also shows `/** */` block docs on the method and `//!` docs on the root. - It checks that HTML in the commentary is escaped. - `justification_can_come_from_docs_or_fenced_commentary_but_not_ordinary_comments` has three cases: docs alone, fenced commentary alone, and an ordinary `//` comment alone. It asserts the `Rust doc comments` and `Citation commentary` headings and that the text appears only when justified. This covers "an ordinary non-doc comment alone does not supply a tracked justification". - **Say so when no tracked justification is present.** The first test asserts `No tracked justification is present.` appears exactly once, for `fn[unexplained]`, and that this entry has no `Rust doc comments` section. The ordinary-comment case in the second test also asserts the message appears. - **Label root citations as file-threshold exception proposals and function or method citations as function exception proposals.** The first test asserts `File-threshold exception proposal` appears exactly once. It asserts `Function exception proposal` appears exactly three times, for the function, the method and the unexplained function. **Possible gaps considered and rejected** - Nothing tests a root citation with no justification. The entry code is shared with function entries and has no root-specific branch for the message, so the function-entry test would catch a failure. - Nothing tests multiple citations on one item. - The requirement does not name multiple citations on one item as a case. No gap is established. There are no `{fixme}` acknowledgments, and none are needed.

text: :::{req} index.file_map.notes.justifications
The view of {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.file_map.notes` MUST show
each `habeas:coverage` citation attached to the file root or an explicitly
declared function or method. Each entry MUST identify its source item and
source location and show the fenced citation commentary and Rust doc comments
supplying its tracked justification under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.exceptions.anchor`.
When no tracked justification is present, the entry MUST say so.
File-root citations MUST be labelled as file-threshold exception proposals;
function and method citations MUST be labelled as function exception proposals,
following {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.exceptions.anchor`.
:::{req} index.file_map.notes
Each listed first-party Rust file path in a combined or per-test file coverage
map MUST link to a file-notes view identifying its workspace-relative path.
:::{req} check.exceptions.anchor
Habeas MUST provide the built-in `habeas:coverage` under
{cite}`requirements.references.builtin_definitions`, with this text:
> Cite this on a source file or explicitly declared function to propose a
> coverage exception. Explain in prose why the item's incomplete execution
> coverage is acceptable. Put the explanation in fenced citation commentary
> or Rust doc comments included in the source item's assessed input. An ordinary
> non-doc comment alone does not supply a tracked justification. The reason
> must be substantive; difficulty alone is not a justification.
> On a file's root item, the exception excuses only
> that file's 80% instrumented-line threshold, including absent measurement
> of its executable code. On an explicit function with a body, it excuses
> that function's recorded zero execution or absence from otherwise usable
> measurement, without excusing the file's threshold.
> The explanation must agree with the current source and any callers or
> configuration assumptions on which it relies. Only a current accepted
> independent assessment permits the exception. A file exception does not
> excuse unexecuted or not-measured functions in that file.
> The citation applies to its source item without conditional build matching
> and may remain when measured coverage satisfies the item's obligations.
Only `{cite}` MAY reference this built-in, inline or fenced using the standard
reference forms of {cite}`requirements.references.roles`. The built-in MUST be
available in every project without a project requirement, site query, or
exception-specific configuration.
